name: @saihm/mcp-server
description: Sovereign, encrypted, sharable, persistent memory protocol MCP server for AI agents. Eight MCP tools forward to a SAIHM operator endpoint that runs the full protocol stack on COTI V2 mainnet.
description_good_justification: README explains: a Model Context Protocol server exposing eight tools that connect any MCP-capable AI agent to a SAIHM operator endpoint running the full sovereign-memory protocol on COTI V2 mainnet.
interact_justification: Public interaction via GitHub Issues at https://github.com/SAIHM-Admin/saihm-mcp/issues. Protocol channel documented at https://saihm.coti.global.
floss_license_justification: Apache-2.0, OSI-approved. LICENSE file at repo root: https://github.com/SAIHM-Admin/saihm-mcp/blob/main/LICENSE.
floss_license_osi_justification: Apache-2.0 is approved by the Open Source Initiative (https://opensource.org/licenses/Apache-2.0).
documentation_basics_justification: README covers install (npm/npx), configure (env vars), wiring into Claude Code, security defaults, and the eight-tool surface.
documentation_interface_justification: README documents each of the eight MCP tools (saihm_remember, saihm_recall, saihm_forget, saihm_status, saihm_share, saihm_revoke_share, saihm_governance_propose, saihm_governance_vote) with input/output expectations and security defaults.
sites_https_justification: All project sites use HTTPS: github.com/SAIHM-Admin/saihm-mcp, www.npmjs.com/package/@saihm/mcp-server, saihm.coti.global.
discussion_justification: GitHub Issues is the primary discussion channel and supports threaded discussion on issues and pull requests.
english_justification: All project artifacts (README, CONTRIBUTING, SECURITY, code comments, commit messages) are in English.
maintained_justification: Actively maintained. v0.1.2 published to npm 2026-05-16; latest commit 2026-05-19. Maintainer responsive (see issues + commit cadence).
no_leaked_credentials_justification: .gitignore excludes all .env* files; no credentials, tokens, or keys are committed. npm publish uses sigstore provenance attestation for distribution integrity.
repo_track_justification: Git on GitHub tracks every change with author, timestamp, and parent commit references.
repo_interim_justification: Work-in-progress is committed to feature branches before merge to main. Main is always releaseable.
repo_distributed_justification: Git is a distributed version control system.
version_unique_justification: npm @saihm/mcp-server@0.1.0 and 0.1.2 are unique semver identifiers; see https://www.npmjs.com/package/@saihm/mcp-server.
release_notes_justification: Release notes captured in tagged commit messages on GitHub: https://github.com/SAIHM-Admin/saihm-mcp/commits/v0.1.2. Major-release commit subject: 'Release v0.1.2: add mcpName, server.json, smithery.yaml'.
release_notes_vulns_justification: No publicly-known vulnerabilities have been disclosed against @saihm/mcp-server to date. The criterion will be applied on first vulnerability-fix release.
report_process_justification: https://github.com/SAIHM-Admin/saihm-mcp/issues for bugs and feature requests. Security issues follow https://github.com/SAIHM-Admin/saihm-mcp/blob/main/SECURITY.md (private channel).
report_responses_justification: Maintainer responds to bug reports within 14 days. SECURITY.md sets a 14-day acknowledgment target for security reports specifically.
enhancement_responses_justification: Maintainer responds to enhancement requests within 14 days. See CONTRIBUTING.md: 'Open an issue first to discuss scope.'
report_archive_justification: GitHub Issues (including closed/resolved) are permanently publicly archived and searchable at https://github.com/SAIHM-Admin/saihm-mcp/issues?q=is%3Aissue.
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: https://github.com/SAIHM-Admin/saihm-mcp/blob/main/SECURITY.md describes the responsible-disclosure process, scope/out-of-scope, and disclosure timelines.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: https://github.com/SAIHM-Admin/saihm-mcp/blob/main/SECURITY.md publishes the private channel architect@saihm.coti.global. Reports are not handled via the public issue tracker.
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: SECURITY.md commits to 14-day acknowledgment and 30-day initial assessment / fix-or-mitigation-plan target for confirmed vulnerabilities, depending on severity and complexity.
build_justification: `npm run build` invokes the TypeScript compiler to emit dist/. See package.json scripts and https://github.com/SAIHM-Admin/saihm-mcp/blob/main/tsconfig.json.
build_common_tools_justification: Standard Node.js + TypeScript toolchain (npm + tsc); no exotic or proprietary build dependencies.
build_floss_tools_justification: All build dependencies are FLOSS: TypeScript (Apache-2.0), npm (Artistic-2.0), Node.js (MIT).
test_justification: Integration test at tests/integration.test.ts. Runnable via `npm test`.
test_invocation_justification: `npm test` documented in README and CONTRIBUTING.md; runnable from a fresh clone after `npm install`.
test_most_justification: Integration test exercises tool listing (tools/list) and each of the eight MCP tool-call round-trips against a mock operator endpoint.
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md: 'New non-trivial functionality must include a test.' Reviewers enforce this on pull requests.
tests_are_added_justification: Test policy applied throughout v0.1.x. Recent v0.1.2 release added metadata only (mcpName, server.json, smithery.yaml) — no functional code path requiring new tests.
tests_documented_added_justification: Test policy documented in CONTRIBUTING.md ('Pull-request process' section).
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions workflow at https://github.com/SAIHM-Admin/saihm-mcp/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml runs `npm ci`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, and `npm test` on every push to main and every pull request, against Node 20.x and 22.x. Workflow runs visible at https://github.com/SAIHM-Admin/saihm-mcp/actions.
warnings_justification: TypeScript strict mode (`strict: true` in tsconfig.json) reports type-correctness and null-safety warnings on every build.
warnings_fixed_justification: Build passes with zero compiler warnings on every commit to main.
warnings_strict_justification: tsconfig.json sets `"strict": true`, enabling all of strictNullChecks, noImplicitAny, strictFunctionTypes, etc.
know_secure_design_justification: Design uses defense-in-depth: HTTPS-only operator endpoints (plain http:// rejected at construction time except 127.0.0.1/localhost dev exception), per-call 30s abort window, 16MB Content-Length cap, no Authorization-header echo on errors, no filesystem reads, zero EVM tooling. Protocol-layer cryptography references well-published primitives: ML-DSA-65 (NIST FIPS-204) for post-quantum identity binding; HKDF (RFC 5869) for per-cell key derivation; standard NIST-approved AEAD ciphers for cell encryption.
know_common_errors_justification: Maintainer is familiar with the OWASP Top 10, the broader OWASP API Security Top 10, and the emerging OWASP-MCP / agent-tool risk taxonomy. Server enforces conservative defaults to prevent credential leakage (no header echo on error, no disk reads, no shell execution).
crypto_published_justification: Operator-endpoint protocol uses publicly-published primitives only: ML-DSA-65 (NIST FIPS-204, 2024), HKDF (RFC 5869, 2010), Ed25519 (RFC 8032, 2017).
crypto_call_justification: MCP server itself implements no cryptography; the operator endpoint runs the full protocol stack. If operators inject signature verifiers via AuthVerifiers, README recommends pure-crypto libraries (@noble/curves, @noble/post-quantum) rather than rolling custom code.
crypto_keylength_justification: ML-DSA-65 is NIST Category 3 (post-quantum); HKDF uses SHA-256; Ed25519 is 256-bit. All meet or exceed NIST 2024+ key-strength recommendations.
crypto_working_justification: No deprecated or broken primitives in use. ML-DSA-65, HKDF, Ed25519 are NIST/IRTF-current recommendations.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: No MD5 or SHA-1 used for integrity; no RC4; no DES; no ECB-mode block ciphers. All hashing is SHA-256 or stronger.
crypto_pfs_justification: Per-cell DEK derivation via canonical HKDF (MPS-PQC-KEY-GEN-v1) ensures session-key separation; KEK rotation is versioned, enabling forward secrecy across rotation boundaries.
crypto_password_storage_justification: @saihm/mcp-server stores no passwords. Authentication uses Bearer tokens issued by the operator after key-bound enrolment; the server forwards these without persisting them.
crypto_random_justification: All randomness sourced from Node.js `crypto.randomBytes`, which uses the OS CSPRNG (/dev/urandom on Linux, CryptGenRandom on Windows).
crypto_used_network_justification: MCP server itself does not negotiate cryptography over the network; it forwards already-authenticated requests over HTTPS to a configured operator endpoint. The operator endpoint implements protocol-layer cryptography end-to-end.
delivery_mitm_justification: Distribution via npm registry over HTTPS with sigstore provenance attestation. Server enforces HTTPS-only on operator endpoint URLs (plain http:// rejected at construction except 127.0.0.1/localhost dev exception).
delivery_unsigned_justification: npm publish flow signs releases via sigstore provenance attestation. Users can verify with `npm audit signatures` and `npm view @saihm/mcp-server --json`.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No known unfixed vulnerabilities in @saihm/mcp-server to date.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No known publicly-disclosed critical vulnerabilities in @saihm/mcp-server to date.
static_analysis_justification: TypeScript strict-mode compilation (`tsc --noEmit`) acts as static analysis on every build and via `npm run typecheck`. The package surface is small (single forwarding shim) with no native code, no SQL, no shell-exec — common static-vuln categories are structurally absent.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: TS strict-mode catches null-deref, type-confusion, and unchecked-undefined classes of bug. Server surface is a small forwarding shim; injection / unsafe-eval / shell-exec attack classes are not present in the call graph.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: All static-analysis warnings are fixed before commits land in main; CI build is clean.
static_analysis_often_justification: Static analysis runs on every build / commit (`tsc --noEmit` integrated into `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build`).
dynamic_analysis_justification: Integration test in tests/integration.test.ts runs the server end-to-end against a mock operator endpoint. Manual smoke-test is required before each npm publish.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: TypeScript on Node.js is a memory-safe runtime; criterion targets memory-unsafe languages (C/C++/Rust-unsafe-blocks/etc.).
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: Integration tests run with assertions enabled (Node.js default). TypeScript strict mode prevents many classes of undefined-behavior at compile-time before runtime checks become necessary.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: All issues uncovered by dynamic testing are fixed before commits land in main.
access_continuity_justification: GOVERNANCE.md describes maintainer add/remove/inactivity-emeritus (12-month inactivity) and removal-for-cause processes plus the foundation-cession path. https://github.com/SAIHM-Admin/saihm-mcp/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
accessibility_best_practices_justificati: MCP server is a stdio-spoken JSON-RPC interface with no human-facing UI; WCAG / ARIA standards do not apply. Tool inputs/outputs are consumed by an AI agent, not by humans directly.
achieve_passing_justification: Project 12898 holds the OpenSSF Best Practices Passing badge at 100% (achieved 2026-05-19). https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects/12898
automated_integration_testing_justificat: GitHub Actions workflow .github/workflows/ci.yml runs the integration test suite (tests/integration.test.ts) via `npm test` on every push to main and every pull request, on Node 20.x and 22.x. https://github.com/SAIHM-Admin/saihm-mcp/actions
build_non_recursive_justification: Build is single-stage `npm run build` (clean + tsc + chmod); no recursive subdirectory builds.
build_preserve_debug_justification: TypeScript build emits .d.ts type-declaration files; sourcemaps can be enabled via tsconfig.json. No debug symbols are stripped.
build_repeatable_justification: Deterministic build: `npm ci` uses package-lock.json for fully-pinned dependencies; tsc emits deterministic output. Re-running `npm ci && npm run build` on the same commit yields identical dist/.
build_standard_variables_justification: Node.js npm project; no make/autoconf install-target convention applies. Standard `npm install` flow is used.
bus_factor_justification: GOVERNANCE.md §'Adding and removing maintainers' plus the inactivity-emeritus and removal-for-cause processes plus the foundation-cession path describe what happens if the founding maintainer becomes unavailable. The protocol specification is mirrored to the IETF Independent Submission Stream (draft-saihm-memory-protocol), so the spec persists independently of the implementation maintainer.
code_of_conduct_justification: Project adopts the Contributor Covenant v2.1 verbatim text at https://github.com/SAIHM-Admin/saihm-mcp/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md. Enforcement contact: architect@saihm.coti.global.
crypto_algorithm_agility_justification: Protocol supports algorithm rotation via KEK versioning (kekVersion field on every cell) and explicit HKDF derivation parameters. New ML-DSA categories or alternative AEAD ciphers can be added without invalidating older cells.
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: Server enforces HTTPS-only operator endpoints; certificate verification is performed by Node.js's default TLS handler, which validates against the system trust store. No insecure-cert bypass is exposed.
crypto_credential_agility_justification: Per-cell DEK derivation via canonical HKDF is keyed off the holder's wallet-bound key material; rotating the wallet key (or the operator-issued auth token) does not invalidate prior cells. Authorization is via Bearer token + key-bound enrolment; tokens are operator-rotatable.
crypto_tls12_justification: Server requires HTTPS for non-localhost endpoints. Node.js's TLS implementation defaults to TLS 1.2+ (TLS 1.3 preferred where supported). Older TLS versions are not negotiated.
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: Verifier private keys are wallet-bound on the holder side; the MCP server itself holds no signing keys and forwards already-authenticated requests without inspecting the holder's private material.
dco_justification: Project requires Developer Certificate of Origin (DCO) 1.1 sign-off on every commit (https://developercertificate.org/). CONTRIBUTING.md documents the requirement at https://github.com/SAIHM-Admin/saihm-mcp/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#licensing-and-dco-sign-off; PRs without `Signed-off-by:` trailers are asked to rebase before merge.
dependency_monitoring_justification: GitHub Dependabot is enabled via .github/dependabot.yml (weekly schedule for npm + github-actions ecosystems). Dependabot opens pull requests for available dependency updates and reports known vulnerabilities. https://github.com/SAIHM-Admin/saihm-mcp/blob/main/.github/dependabot.yml
documentation_current_justification: README is updated with every release. The README documents the current v0.1.2 surface (eight tools, configuration, security defaults, achievements, roadmap, dependencies). The CHANGELOG.md tracks release history.
documentation_quick_start_justification: README's 'Install' + 'Configure' + 'Wire into Claude Code' sections provide a quick-start path from zero to a working server in under five minutes. https://github.com/SAIHM-Admin/saihm-mcp/blob/main/README.md
documentation_security_justification: SECURITY.md describes the vulnerability disclosure process, private channel, scope/out-of-scope, and protocol-layer cryptography. README's 'Security' section documents the server's HTTPS-only, content-length cap, and abort-window defaults. GOVERNANCE.md describes security-sensitive-change review.
governance_justification: GOVERNANCE.md at https://github.com/SAIHM-Admin/saihm-mcp/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md documents the project's governance: roles (Contributor / Maintainer / Founding Maintainer / TSC-when-formed), decision process for specification vs implementation vs releases, maintainer add/remove/inactivity, conflict resolution, code review, intellectual property and trademark.
implement_secure_design_justification: Secure-design defaults documented in README §Security: HTTPS-only operator endpoints, per-call 30s abort window, 16 MB Content-Length cap, no Authorization-header echo on errors, no filesystem reads, zero EVM tooling. CONTRIBUTING.md disallows introducing new cryptographic primitives in the MCP-server repo (protocol-stack-only).
input_validation_justification: Server validates SAIHM_ENDPOINT_URL at construction (HTTPS-only enforcement except 127.0.0.1/localhost dev exception); response Content-Length is capped at 16 MB; Authorization header is never echoed in error messages. TypeScript strict mode adds compile-time validation across the call surface.
installation_common_justification: Standard npm install: `npm install @saihm/mcp-server` or `npx @saihm/mcp-server`. Documented in README §Install.
installation_development_quick_justifica: From a fresh git clone: `npm install && npm run build && npm test` reproduces a working dev environment in under two minutes (assuming Node 20.x or 22.x). Documented in CONTRIBUTING.md.
installation_standard_variables_justific: Node.js npm project; no GNU autoconf-style install variables (DESTDIR, prefix, etc.) apply. Installation uses npm's standard mechanism.
interfaces_current_justification: Project interfaces conform to current standards: Model Context Protocol (current spec), Node.js LTS (20.x + 22.x), TypeScript 5.x, npm registry conventions, MCP Registry / Smithery metadata schemas. No deprecated APIs used.
internationalization_justification: MCP server's user-visible text (tool inputs/outputs) is consumed by AI agents, which handle localization at the agent layer. The server's own error messages are technical and English-only by design; localization is not a use-case for this layer.
maintenance_or_update_justification: Updates flow through standard npm: `npm update @saihm/mcp-server`. SemVer is followed: minor releases are non-breaking; major releases follow the breaking-change process in GOVERNANCE.md.
roles_responsibilities_justification: GOVERNANCE.md §Roles clearly states authority for Contributor, Maintainer, Founding Maintainer, and TSC (when formed). The founding maintainer holds final say until a TSC is constituted (planned on AAIF acceptance or earliest cross-org maintainer).
signed_releases_justification: npm publish uses sigstore provenance attestation; users verify with `npm audit signatures` and inspect `npm view @saihm/mcp-server --json | jq .dist`. README §Security documents the verification procedure.
sites_password_security_justification: @saihm/mcp-server stores no passwords; the protocol uses key-bound enrolment with operator-issued Bearer tokens. No password fields exist anywhere in the surface.
test_policy_mandated_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md mandates that 'New non-trivial functionality must include a test'; this is enforced in PR review. Reviewers reject PRs that add behavior without corresponding test coverage.
updateable_reused_components_justificati: Dependencies are tracked in package.json + package-lock.json. Dependabot monitors weekly and opens PRs for updates. `npm outdated` shows the current update surface.
version_tags_signed_justification: Going forward, git tags are GPG-signed via `git tag -s` per the maintainer's local GPG key. The v0.1.2 tag predates this policy; v0.1.3 and subsequent tags will be signed.
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio: SECURITY.md §Disclosure commits to crediting the reporter (with permission) in the advisory and release notes. https://github.com/SAIHM-Admin/saihm-mcp/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_response_process_justifica: SECURITY.md publishes the response process: 14-day acknowledgment, 30-day initial assessment + fix-or-mitigation-plan target. Disclosure follows a coordinated-disclosure model. https://github.com/SAIHM-Admin/saihm-mcp/blob/main/SECURITY.md
documentation_architecture_justification: ARCHITECTURE.md at https://github.com/SAIHM-Admin/saihm-mcp/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md documents the high-level architecture: project scope, system diagram, components (MCP tool surface, runtime client, types, reporting, tests), data envelope, trust model, threat-model summary, build/test/release flow, and anti-overreach principles.
hardening_justification: HARDENING.md at https://github.com/SAIHM-Admin/saihm-mcp/blob/main/HARDENING.md collects enforced hardening choices: HTTPS-only transport, TLS 1.2+, no Authorization-header echo on errors, 30s abort window, 16 MB Content-Length cap, no filesystem reads, no EVM tooling, signed npm releases (sigstore provenance), pinned dependencies, Dependabot, DCO requirement, signed git tags going forward, eight-tool cap as protocol-invariant surface minimization. Each choice is enforced in code or in the published artifact, not aspirational.
documentation_roadmap_justification: README §Roadmap publishes the 12-month roadmap: 2026-Q2 operator-endpoint reference + OpenSSF Silver pursuit; 2026-Q3 first 2-3 external organization deployments + AAIF Project Proposal submission gate; 2026-Q4 NIST AI RMF crosswalk public review + EU AI Act compliance-checklist generator + OpenSSF Silver award target; 2027-Q1 IETF RFC publication + v1.0 reference implementation. https://github.com/SAIHM-Admin/saihm-mcp/blob/main/README.md#roadmap
documentation_achievements_justification: README §Achievements lists the project's current standards-track credentials: OpenSSF BP Passing badge (project 12898, 2026-05-19), IETF ISE draft-saihm-memory-protocol-00 acceptance (2026-05-18), npm registry @saihm/mcp-server@0.1.2 (2026-05-16), MCP Registry / Glama listing (2026-05-16). https://github.com/SAIHM-Admin/saihm-mcp/blob/main/README.md#achievements
external_dependencies_justification: README §Dependencies lists the runtime + build dependencies and their licenses (Node.js MIT, @modelcontextprotocol/sdk MIT, TypeScript Apache-2.0, tsx MIT). No copyleft, no proprietary dependencies. Operator-side recommended primitive libraries (@noble/curves MIT, @noble/post-quantum MIT) are also enumerated. https://github.com/SAIHM-Admin/saihm-mcp/blob/main/README.md#dependencies
coding_standards_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md §Coding conventions documents the project's coding standards: TypeScript with ES modules, strict mode, minimal MCP-server surface (thin forwarding shim), no new cryptographic primitives in this repository, no ninth MCP tool (protocol-invariant cap). https://github.com/SAIHM-Admin/saihm-mcp/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#coding-conventions
assurance_case_justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md at https://github.com/SAIHM-Admin/saihm-mcp/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md presents a Claims-Arguments-Evidence (CAE) structured argument that the project's security claims hold under its documented threat model. Five top-level goals (G1 credential confidentiality, G2 availability under adversarial input, G3 distribution integrity, G4 cryptographic primitives publicly-validated and current, G5 process controls prevent unauthorized changes) each have arguments, evidence rows, and residual-risk acknowledgments. Counterarguments are considered and dismissed or scoped. An independent-reviewer verification checklist is appended.
regression_tests_added50_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md §Pull-request process step 4 mandates that every bug-fix PR must include a regression test that would have caught the bug (i.e., fails on the pre-fix code, passes on the post-fix code). PRs that fix a reported bug without a corresponding regression test are asked to add one before merge. Documentation-only and metadata-only fixes are exempt. https://github.com/SAIHM-Admin/saihm-mcp/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#pull-request-process
